key_insight: Mac-Diff is a conditional diffusion model that uses locality-aware cross-modal attention to generate diverse, realistic conformational ensembles for unseen proteins, capturing both local flexibility and global structural heterogeneity.
problem_solved: Standard structure predictors produce single or limited conformations and fail to represent protein dynamic ensembles and heterogeneity, limiting downstream tasks that require realistic conformational variability.
method: Conditional diffusion generative model that produces full conformational ensembles conditioned on protein inputs (e.g., sequence or template features).

Locality-aware cross-modal attention aligns and integrates information across modalities (local motifs, geometry, chemical features) to preserve physical local structure while enabling global diversity.
Sampling and training objectives designed to encourage ensemble diversity and realism (diversity-promoting losses and reconstruction/consistency terms).
impact: Provides ML researchers and practitioners a practical generative framework to model protein dynamics and uncertainty, improving applications like drug design, functional annotation, and simulation-informed predictions by producing realistic ensembles rather than single static structures.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: conditional diffusion pipeline with locality-aware cross-modal attention blocks and conditioning inputs.
Before/after ensemble visualization: single static structure vs. diverse conformational ensemble for the same protein.
Quantitative comparison chart: diversity & accuracy metrics (e.g., RMSD distribution, ensemble coverage) comparing Mac-Diff to baselines.
Attention heatmap overlaid on protein structure showing locality-aware modal alignment of motifs/features.
paper_title: Conditional diffusion with locality-aware modal alignment for generating diverse protein conformational ensembles
paper_authors: Baoli Wang, Chenglin Wang, Jingyang Chen, Danlin Liu, Changzhi Sun
